title: Integral factor recovery
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$ and
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix an indeterminate $T$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. For every prime
$\ell\neq p$, let
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and, for $P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for its coefficientwise
extension, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Define the
point-count zeta series by

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})\frac{T^n}{n}\right),
$$

and write its
normalized reduced integral
presentation as

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\frac{A(T)}{B(T)},\qquad
A,B\in\mathbf Z[T],\quad A(0)=B(0)=1,
\quad\gcd(A,B)=1\text{ in }\mathbf Q[T].
$$

For every prime $\ell\neq p$, define the
odd and even parity products

$$
N_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\i\text{ odd}}}P_{i,\ell}(T),
\qquad
D_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\i\text{ even}}}P_{i,\ell}(T).
$$

There are unique polynomials

$$
P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]
\qquad(0\leq i\leq2d)
$$

with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every
$\ell\neq p$. These are the
integral Frobenius factors.
For every $\ell\neq p$,

$$
A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell,
\qquad
B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell.
$$

The resulting factors satisfy

$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T),
$$

and

$$
\deg P_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)
$$

where $H^i(X,\Ql)$ denotes the
ordinary cohomology group,
for every $\ell\neq p$.

proof.text:
*Step 1: existence of the integral factors.* Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$. For every prime $\ell\neq p$ choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$ and, by [lem-weil-realization-exists], an $\ell$-adic realization $\jmath_\ell:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}\subset\Qlb$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure-q]. With these choices, and with $(A,B)$ as the chosen normalized reduced integral presentation of $Z(X_0,T)$, [thm-weil-realization-independence] provides, for every $0\leq i\leq2d$, a polynomial $Q_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $Q_i(0)=1$ such that, for every $\ell\neq p$,

$$
Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}(T)=P_{i,\ell}(T)\quad\text{in }\Qlb[T],
$$

where $Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}$ is the coefficientwise extension of $Q_i$ along $\jmath_\ell$ and $P_{i,\ell}\in\Ql[T]$ [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] is viewed in $\Qlb[T]$ through the inclusion $\Ql\subset\Qlb$. Since $\jmath_\ell$ fixes every integer [lem-weil-realization-exists], $Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}$ is the image of $Q_i$ under $\mathbf Z[T]\to\Qlb[T]$, $c\mapsto c\cdot1_{\Qlb}$, which is the coefficientwise extension $Q_i\mapsto Q_i^{(\ell)}\in\Ql[T]$ [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension] followed by the inclusion $\Ql[T]\subset\Qlb[T]$. That inclusion is injective [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective], so $Q_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ in $\Ql[T]$. Put $P_i=Q_i$. Then $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $P_i(0)=1$, and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every prime $\ell\neq p$: $P_i$ is an integral realization-independent factor in degree $i$ [def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor]. This is the existence clause.

source.place: §1, Théorème (1.6) and 'Preuve de (1.7) ⇒ (1.6)', pp. 276–277 (paper pagination; PDF pp. 4–5): 'La description ci-dessus des racines de $P_i(t)$ est indépendante de $\ell$; le polynôme $P_i(t)$ lui-même est donc indépendant de $\ell$'; the derivation of the integral $P_i$ is thm-weil-realization-independence, this step only reads its conclusion. Blueprint: literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-intfactors/prop-integral-recovery.md, '## Proof', first sentence.

proof.text:
*Step 2: uniqueness.* Let $(P_i')_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be polynomials in $\mathbf Z[T]$ with $P_i'(0)=1$ and $P_i'^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every prime $\ell
eq p$. Choose one prime $\ell
eq p$ (there are infinitely many primes). Then $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}=P_i'^{(\ell)}$ in $\Ql[T]$ by Step 1. The ring homomorphism $\mathbf Z	o\Ql$ is injective because $\Ql$ has characteristic zero [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero], so the coefficientwise extension $\mathbf Z[T]	o\Ql[T]$, $P\mapsto P^{(\ell)}$ [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension], is injective [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective]; hence $P_i'=P_i$. (The normalization $P_i'(0)=1$ is not needed for this.) So the $P_i$ of Step 1 are the unique polynomials in $\mathbf Z[T]$ with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell
eq p$; these are the integral Frobenius factors.

source.place: \begin{proposition}[Integral factor recovery] \label{prop:integral-recovery}, lines 3154–3181: the uniqueness clause 'If another family $(\widetilde P_i)$ in $\mathbf Z[T]$ has constant term one and the same realizations for all primes $\ell\neq p$, then $\widetilde P_i=P_i$'. The master blueprint (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-intfactors/prop-integral-recovery.md, '## Proof') asserts uniqueness in its first sentence without argument.

proof.text:
*Step 3: the parity products are the scalar extensions of $A$ and $B$.* The pair $(A,B)$ is, by hypothesis, a normalized reduced integral presentation of $Z(X_0,T)$ [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction]: $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $A(0)=B(0)=1$, $\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$ and $Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T)$ as a Taylor series at $T=0$. This is exactly the chosen presentation for which [thm-weil-realization-independence] is stated, and its parity-product clause gives, for every prime $\ell\neq p$,

$$
A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell,\qquad B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell\quad\text{in }\Ql[T],
$$

with $N_\ell=\prod_{i\text{ odd}}P_{i,\ell}$ and $D_\ell=\prod_{i\text{ even}}P_{i,\ell}$ the odd and even parity products [def-weil-parity-products] and $A^{(\ell)},B^{(\ell)}$ the coefficientwise extensions [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension]. This is the parity-product clause of the statement.

source.place: §1, 'Preuve de (1.7) ⇒ (1.6)', pp. 276–277 (PDF pp. 4–5): $Z(X_0,t)=P/Q$ with $P,Q\in\mathbf Z[t]$ coprime of constant term $1$ (Fatou), the $P_i$ pairwise coprime, hence '$P(t)=\prod_{i\text{ impair}}P_i(t)$, $Q(t)=\prod_{i\text{ pair}}P_i(t)$'; in the DAG this is the parity-product clause of thm-weil-realization-independence. Blueprint: literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-intfactors/prop-integral-recovery.md, '## Proof': 'uniqueness of the normalized fraction gives $A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell$ and $B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell$'.

proof.text:
*Step 4: the integral factorization in $\mathbf Q(T)$.* Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$. The coefficientwise extension $\mathbf Z[T]\to\Ql[T]$ is a ring homomorphism [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective], so by Step 1, [def-weil-parity-products] and Step 3,

$$
\Bigl(\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ odd}}}P_i\Bigr)^{(\ell)}
=\prod_{i\text{ odd}}P_i^{(\ell)}
=\prod_{i\text{ odd}}P_{i,\ell}=N_\ell=A^{(\ell)},
\qquad
\Bigl(\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ even}}}P_i\Bigr)^{(\ell)}
=\prod_{i\text{ even}}P_{i,\ell}=D_\ell=B^{(\ell)}.
$$

Since $\Ql$ has characteristic zero [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero], the extension $\mathbf Z[T]\to\Ql[T]$ [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension] is injective [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective], hence

$$
A=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ odd}}}P_i,
\qquad
B=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ even}}}P_i
\qquad\text{in }\mathbf Z[T].
$$

By [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction], $Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T)$ as a Taylor series at $T=0$, that is, $Z(X_0,T)$ is the expansion of the rational function $A/B\in\mathbf Q(T)$ ($B(0)=1$, so $B$ is invertible in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$). Substituting the two products and writing the even factors, which are in the denominator, with exponent $-1=(-1)^{i+1}$ and the odd ones with exponent $+1=(-1)^{i+1}$,

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\frac{\prod_{i\text{ odd}}P_i(T)}{\prod_{i\text{ even}}P_i(T)}
=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T).
$$

This is the factorization clause.

source.place: Summary 27.14 (b) and (d) with Theorem 27.6 and Proposition 27.11, pp. 156–159 (PDF pp. 162–165, v2.21): $Z(X_0,t)=P_1P_3\cdots P_{2d-1}/P_0P_2\cdots P_{2d}$ with the $P_{r}\in1+t\mathbf Z[t]$ independent of $\ell$, numerator and denominator of the reduced form of $Z$ in $\mathbf Z[t]$. Deligne, literature/deligne-weil-I_PMIHES-1974-43.pdf, p. 277: '$P(t)=\prod_{i\text{ impair}}P_i(t)$, $Q(t)=\prod_{i\text{ pair}}P_i(t)$'. Blueprint: literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-intfactors/prop-integral-recovery.md, '## Proof': 'Thus ... $Z(X_0,T)=\prod P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ after scalar extension', where the descent from $\Ql[T]$ to $\mathbf Z[T]$ is left unsaid.

proof.text:
*Step 5: the degrees.* Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$. Since $\mathbf Z\to\Ql$ is injective [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero], the coefficientwise extension [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension] preserves degrees [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-degree]: $\deg P_i=\deg P_i^{(\ell)}=\deg P_{i,\ell}$, the last equality by Step 1. Now $P_{i,\ell}=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$ [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] is the reverse characteristic polynomial [def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial] of the endomorphism $F_{i,\ell}$ of $V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, the ordinary cohomology group [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. By [prop-cohomological-finiteness] (applied with $E=\Ql$ to the proper $X_0$), $H^i(X,\Ql)$ is finite-dimensional over $\Ql$ and the geometric Frobenius $F_{i,\ell}$ on it is an automorphism, hence invertible; the definition of the family records that these two facts are that proposition. Therefore, by [lem-weil-reverse-charpoly-coefficients] (3), $\deg P_{i,\ell}=\dim_{\Ql}V_{i,\ell}$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Altogether

$$
\deg P_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)\qquad\text{for every prime }\ell\neq p,
$$

which is the degree clause; in particular the right-hand side does not depend on $\ell$.

source.place: Summary 27.14 (e), p. 159 (PDF p. 165, v2.21): '$\beta_r=\deg P_r(t)$', with Theorem 27.6 ($P_r(X,t)=\det(1-Ft\mid H^r(X,\mathbf Q_\ell))$) and Remark 27.7. Blueprint: literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-intfactors/prop-integral-recovery.md, '## Proof': 'The degree of $P_{i,\ell}$ is $\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)$ by [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]; scalar extension preserves degree', where the invertibility of $F_{i,\ell}$ that the degree needs is left unsaid.

proof_origin.place: ## Proof; the result is Deligne, literature/deligne-weil-I_PMIHES-1974-43.pdf, Théorème (1.6) with 'Preuve de (1.7) ⇒ (1.6)', pp. 276–277, and Milne, literature/milne-lectures-on-etale-cohomology_LEC.pdf, Summary 27.14 (b), (d), (e), p. 159, which the steps cite; the division of the argument between thm-weil-realization-independence and this node is the blueprint's, so the proof as a whole follows the blueprint's one-paragraph proof, expanded

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against the blueprint source (identical on master; slopmaster2 has no node file, its TeX proposition prop:integral-recovery states the same four clauses, with the uniqueness clause spelled out) and against Deligne Weil I (1.6)/(1.7 ⇒ 1.6), pp. 276–277, and Milne LEC 27.14 (b),(d),(e); kept the statement. The imported one-paragraph proof was replaced by five steps: existence of the P_i read off from thm-weil-realization-independence (which needs an ℓ-adic realization to exist and the descent of an identity from Qlb[T] to Q_ℓ[T]), uniqueness (injectivity of Z[T]→Q_ℓ[T], asserted by the blueprint without argument), the parity-product clause (the theorem's conclusion for the chosen presentation), the factorization in Q(T) (descent of A^(ℓ)=N_ℓ, B^(ℓ)=D_ℓ to A=∏_odd P_i, B=∏_even P_i in Z[T], left unsaid by the blueprint), and the degree clause (degree preserved under coefficientwise extension; deg P_{i,ℓ}=dim V_{i,ℓ} needs F_{i,ℓ} invertible, which is prop-cohomological-finiteness, and the degree lemma lem-weil-reverse-charpoly-coefficients created by another worker). Moved the nine imported definition citations from the proof to stmt_deps (the statement, not the proof, uses them) and added def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-coefficientwise-extension, def-weil-vector-space-dimension for Z[T], P^(ℓ) and dim; def-weil-finite-field-fiber and def-weil-geometric-hypotheses are statement dependencies only. Created four Mathlib leaves: lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective (Polynomial.map_injective), lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-degree (Polynomial.natDegree_map_eq_of_injective), lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero (Int.cast_injective, CharZero ℚ_[p]), lem-weil-realization-exists (IsAlgClosure.equiv with algebraicClosure.isAlgClosure). The pair (A,B) is read as any normalized reduced integral presentation (as in thm-weil-realization-independence); its existence and uniqueness is prop-weil-zeta-normalized-presentation, not needed by the proof.
